# PR #3636: Patch: a job ran over 7 minutes

Closes #3629

## What changed and why

`web (unit 2/8)` ran 8m 48s against the 5-minute target, and `[web] unit` is already at the 8-shard maximum, so no count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` can split it. The shard's weight was three full-history walks in two files. Each now runs per pull request over a constant 9 snapshots (the first six plus the newest three, mirroring the #3418 precedent in `source.test.ts`), and the full-history walk moved to `daily()`:

- [diff.test.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill-2/_work/_temp/work/item-3629/apps/web/src/patches/diff.test.ts): the `:295` walk split into a bounded `it` (2.4 s, was 64 s) and a `daily` full walk with its original `R388` title.
- [placeholders.test.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill-2/_work/_temp/work/item-3629/apps/web/src/patches/placeholders.test.tsx): the `:53` and `:77` walks split the same way. Bounded change walk is 1.3 s (was 68 s). Bounded face walk is ~54 s on a slow box: nine snapshots still draw 2730 faces, but it no longer grows with history.
- No test deleted, emptied, or renamed out of R388. Untouched: `.github/`, `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, `bot/`, spec, catalog, and Rust files (`git status` shows only the two test files).

## How tested

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/diff.test.ts` — 22 passed, 1 skipped (daily), 9.35 s total.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/placeholders.test.tsx` — 3 passed, 2 skipped (dailies), 68.7 s total.
- `JACKIOH_DAILY=1 ... diff.test.ts -t "every card every patch"` — full walk passes, 64 s.
- `JACKIOH_DAILY=1 ... placeholders.test.tsx -t "every change of every card"` — full walk passes (68 s) plus bounded (1.3 s).
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both files — clean. `cargo fmt --check` — clean. `cargo jackioh spec check` — ok (1888 rulings, 4895 proofs).
- The `every face` full walk was not re-run locally: the planner recorded its worker OOM at 178 s on this shared machine as environmental (it passes on CI runners), and it runs nowhere per-PR now.

- Bounded face walk gets `EVERY_SNAPSHOT_MS` (180 s), not the planned 60 s. Measured 59.3 s then an actual 60 s timeout failure on this machine, so 60 s has zero headroom and flakes. Same body, read set, and assertions as planned. Rejected alternative: shrinking the read set (e.g. newest-only or changed-cards-only) would hit seconds but breaks the first-six/newest-three shape the plan shares with `source.test.ts` and drops brief-era face shapes per-PR.
- The `:77` daily walk uses `EVERY_SNAPSHOT_MS` instead of its old 60 s timeout, since it is a new daily-only test over all 151 snapshots. Rejected: keeping 60 s, which the full walk demonstrably exceeds (68 s).
- `EVERY_SNAPSHOT_MS` comment shortened from `source.test.ts`'s wording, which names these two files and would be self-referential here.

## Person ask (the bot may not edit `.github/`)

In `.github/workflows/super.yml`, job `web-extra`, append the two files to the vitest path list so the moved daily walks actually run daily:

- before: `pnpm exec vitest run --project web src/audio/ src/fx/ src/cards/art/convention.test.ts src/net/promote-production.test.ts src/net/promote-staging.test.ts src/tutorial/scripts/`
- after: the same line plus ` src/patches/diff.test.ts src/patches/placeholders.test.tsx`

(The same line could also take `src/patches/source.test.ts`, whose #3418 `daily` cases likewise run nowhere today.)

## Reviewer, look twice

- The bounded face walk at ~54 s is the shard's remaining lump. It is O(1) in history length, but catalog growth still grows it. If shard 2/8 stays near 5 minutes, that walk is where to cut next.
- The three `daily()` walks run nowhere until the person ask above lands — the same standing gap #3418 left. R388 per-PR rests on the bounded cases plus the Rust `patches.rs` snapshot test cited in the `daily:` reason.
